Subject: Questions on AWS metering & entitlements for Redwood Inference SaaS

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team is excited. Procurement asked me to put together a couple of technical/contract questions so we can finalize our billing flow for Redwood delivered via AWS Marketplace. High level: we want to understand how our Acme product SKUs map to Marketplace entitlements, how usage metering will flow to our AWS bill, and which contract (Acmeâ€™s SaaS contract vs. AWS Marketplace contract) drives invoicing and refunds.

Specific questions:
- Do we need to onboard as a SaaS SaaS-Subscriptions listing or SaaS Metering? Which model supports monthly per-seat billing with seat-count changes mid-billing-cycle?
- What fields do you expect in the entitlement payload? We have internal SKU codes and region tags that must be preserved in reports.
- Who owns taxes and refunds when Marketplace is enabled (Redwood or Acme)?
- Any data retention / audit logs Redwood can provide for SOC/finance?

I've attached a CSV that shows our SKU mapping proposal (acme-entitlement-mapping.csv). Can your team review and propose a minimal payload example we can test?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — procurement hopes to close by 1/22.

Best,
Maria Gomez
Procurement Manager
Acme Health

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Questions on AWS metering & entitlements for Redwood Inference SaaS

Hi Maria — thanks for the clear list. I looped in Ben (marketplace ops) and Lauren (partnerships) to make sure we cover legal/ops and go-to-market requirements. Below are short answers and an action plan.

Quick answers: 
- Recommendation: Use the AWS Marketplace SaaS Subscriptions (with Metering API enabled). That supports subscription lifecycle and metered usage reporting. For monthly per-seat billing with mid-cycle changes, you can report prorated usage via the metering API; we also support sending entitlement updates to match your SKU -> product_code mapping.
- Entitlement payload: we typically expect product_code (Marketplace listing id), customer_identifier (your account id), quantity, timestamp, metadata (free-form key:value for region/sku). I attached an integration guide pull from our notes (aws-marketplace-integration-guide.pdf) and a sample JSON snippet in the attached CSV comments.
- Taxes/refunds: Marketplace generally handles billing and tax collection on the AWS invoice. Redwood will coordinate refunds for usage errors via AWS purchase flow (we provide reconciliation and request refunds through Marketplace APIs). Final terms will be reflected in the SaaS contract & marketplace listing docs.
- Audit logs: Redwood can provide per-customer metering logs, reconciliation reports, and tokenized request traces for the retention period required by SOC 2.

Action plan (next 10 business days):
1) Ben to review your CSV and propose the exact product_code mapping and a test tenant. (Ben)
2) Acme DevOps to provide a test AWS account id and a sample seat-change scenario we can simulate. (Acme)
3) Redwood to provide a small test harness and example payloads (we will share a test webhook endpoint and reconciliation CSV).
4) We schedule a walkthrough w/ AWS partner manager if there are Marketplace-specific gating items. (Lauren will coordinate)

Let us know timelines — we should be able to deliver the first test payload within 3 business days.

Karthik Iyer

Hi Maria & team,

Thanks for including AWS. Quick notes from the Marketplace side:
- SaaS (Subscriptions) + Metering APIs will support what you describe. You should provision a product_code for each billing product (e.g., ACME-REDFEAT-PERSEAT) and pass that as product_code in all metering submissions.
- Recommended minimal metering payload: {product_code, customer_aws_account_id, dimension (e.g. seats), quantity, timestamp, meta: {acme_sku, region}}. Metadata is preserved in the reporting exports.
- Proration: send the actual quantity each day; Marketplace will handle prorated billing when subscriptions change mid-month. Alternatively, report increments/decrements via the usage records API.
- Refunds: AWS handles customer refunds on the invoice; partners may request reimbursements via the partner refund process. We'll share the partner reimbursements runbook if needed.

I'll schedule a short sync with Redwood and Acme DevOps to approve the test plan and confirm the Marketplace test account. Proposed window: Mon 1/12 or Tue 1/13 morning PT.

Regards,
